newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - AT&T's blue chip image tarnished.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - AT&T's blue chip image tarnished.

text.p: The ongoing assault on AT&T Corp's core long-distance telephone business by smaller rivals has hammered the stock, and its reputation as a blue chip investment "safe" enough for orphans and widows.
Shares of the most widely held issue in America lost 1/8 to 51-3/8 Wednesday afternoon. AT&T tumbled 5-5/8 Tuesday after warning of an earnings shortfall for the second half.
"It's year-high was 68-7/8 on February 14. It's been a Valentine's Day massacre in slow motion," said Ken Tower, a technical analyst at UST Securities, of the stock's slide.
In contrast, since mid-February the Dow industrials have climbed five percent. AT&T is a Dow component.

"Telephone was a widows and orphan stock, but they changed the rules when they decided to aggressively split the company into three divisions. They've had some key management defections and ... question marks about the efficacy of their business splits," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. AT&T spun off telecom equipment maker Lucent Technologies Inc and the last part of the three-way split will be around year-end when shareholders receive stock in computing company NCR.
Although AT&T shares are now hovering near their three-year lows of 49-50, market analysts saw few reasons for investors to jump in now.

Even before Tuesday's earnings warning, "the stock already looked lousy from our point of view," Tower said. "The only good news is we haven't made a lower low, after falling to 49-1/4 July 24. If we hold the July lows here then it simply puts AT&T in a big trading range."
Paul Rabbitt, a quantitative analyst at Oppenheimer & Co, said, "It's not a good value or growth situation at 14 times earnings and eight percent earnings growth."
"Technically, it's got poor relative strength and was in a downtrend before the news," Rabbitt added.

"For investors looking for some dividend yield and conservative big caps, the reasonable area would be non-durables, big pharmaceutivals or food companies, or the energy area with inventories low and a seasonal play," he said.

Rabbitt said AT&T was the least compelling stock among its competitors, "while Ameritech (Corp, unchanged at 54-1/4) was the most attractive as a hold. But the Baby Bells have had new lows, declining lows and declining highs."

Among the bells, SBC Communications Inc lost 1/4 to 48-1/4, Bell Atlantic Corp rose 1/4 to 59, GTE Corp was unchanged at 38-1/2, U S West Communications Group was unchanged at 29-3/4, NYNEX Corp fell 1/8 to 43-5/8, BellSouth Corp was off 1/2 to 37, MCI Communications Corp was unchanged at 26-1/4, Sprint Corp added 1/4 to 40 and Pacific Telesis Group slipped 3/8 to 33-1/2.
Analysts said investors may want to view AT&T shares differently now, as a trading opportunity rather than a buy and hold stock.
"People should consider it as a trading stock rather than a stock with great potential. It's a different-looking stock from past years," Tower said.
Rabbitt said if the stock held 49, "it should be able to bounce, similar to what it did in July. It could bounce to 55."

Value Line's Orlando said, "Investors have to be more selective. This is a good argument for portfolio diversification if even the bluest of the blues like Telephone can sneeze and have the retail investors contract pneumonia."
